searchText: So given that a validator may sometimes be selected to produce more than 1 block in a single epoch, and that the randao_reveal is that validator's signature over the epoch number - does that mean the second block they produce would have the exact same randao_reveal and thus be predictable? I can't imagine it would have any material effect on the amount of randomness but seemed interesting... sounds correcct so the `randao_reveal` should either sign over the slot or we say that the chances of this happening are so low, it isn't worth updating the spec someone calculated this somewhere with 1348 validators it was something like once in 6 months statistically.. not sure if thats 100% right, but that doesn't sound that low... <@!144468805697929216> Did the math over on the Prysm discord: "This gives us an expectation that we will have a validator with more than one proposal slots in an epoch roughly every 6.5 years. Not high, but not 0 either." I suspect missing blocks will have much more impact on randomness than proposing twice in an epoch. that's it! ok 6 months was way off :/ thanks adrian Probably only need to change if we ever introduce penalties for revealing your randao too early.
